mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to bring this all together. Healing from shame and trauma? It’s never a straight line. Sometimes it’s slow, sometimes messy, but each step forward counts. Living authentically takes real courage—especially when there’s a risk of being misunderstood or turned away. And forgiveness? That’s something you give yourself. It’s not about excusing the hurt, but about letting go for your own peace. Families and faith—they can change over time, even when old scars still linger. And don’t forget, sharing your story can be powerful. It can spark change, create connection, and remind someone else that they’re not alone. The story behind “Boy Erased” isn’t just one person’s struggle—it’s a reminder for anyone who’s ever felt out of place or unsure about who they are. The road to self-acceptance is rarely easy. There’ll be setbacks, doubts, and days when the weight of the past feels overwhelming. But here’s the hope: healing doesn’t mean pretending the pain never happened. It means learning how to live with it, forgiving yourself and others, and building a life that feels true to you. So, if you’re wrestling with similar questions, know this—you’re not alone. Every single step you take, no matter how small, matters. Reach out for support. When you’re ready, share your story. And always remember—your value isn’t defined by anyone else’s expectations. The world needs your voice, your courage, and your compassion. Keep going. This journey is yours to shape, and there’s room for you—exactly as you are.
